newsitem.title: UK: Intellectuals vote Churchill greatest European.
newsitem.headline: Intellectuals vote Churchill greatest European.

text.p: An international panel of intellectuals voted British war-time leader Winston Churchill the most outstanding European of the 20th century, a magazine reported on Wednesday.
The survey for the first edition of the Europe Quarterly, a new social and cultural magazine, included politicians, scientists, artists and politicians from 24 countries in Europe.

The former British prime minister beat physicist Albert Einstein, who was second in the poll. Doctors Francis Crick and James Watson, the team that discovered the structure of DNA, Sigmund Freud, the father of psychoanalysis, Pope John Paul II and the artist Pablo Picasso all shared third place.
"I am surprised by the outcome," editor Maggie Lennon said in a statement.
"I expected a bigger show for the civilising forces of writing and the creative arts, but the jury has interpreted more in terms of sheer survival.
"Despite all the talks about a new Europe, it seems the continent is still profoundly influenced by the effects of the Second World War," she added.
Soviet physicist and human rights campaigner Andrei Sakharov, the former leader of the Soviet Union Mikhail Gorbachev and Austrian philosopher Karl Popper shared seventh place.
Former British prime minister Margaret Thatcher was the only woman to be nominated in the poll. She received one vote.
